results.name: Stylized Food & Cafe Props Pack
results.description:
Stylized low-poly 3D pack is perfect for mobile, VR, and casual games. Includes all the essentials for a fun cafe or fast-food scene: burgers, donuts, fries, sauces, drinks, a POS terminal, a reserved sign, a bell, and more.

Flexible modular models - for example, burgers with separate layers - lettuce, cheese, patty, and buns can be swapped, removed, or rearranged.

File formats: Each model comes in FBX format, plus Blender file with all assets.

Textures: 5 textures total, 2048×2048, PBR-ready.

Optimized for games: Low-poly, stylized models with clean geometry - perfect for mobile, VR, and casual game projects.

Ready to use: All assets are properly grouped and named, making integration into Unity, Unreal, or other engines seamless.

results.name: Cash register
results.description:
A detailed 3D model of a modern electronic cash register (POS terminal) used in supermarkets, grocery stores, and retail outlets. This model is designed to be a central prop for checkout area visualizations or shop simulators.

Design: Realistic interface with a digital display, functional-looking keypad, and integrated receipt printer.

Optimization: Balanced polygon count, suitable for both close-up renders and as part of a larger store environment.

Use Cases: Perfect for game environments, architectural visualization of commercial spaces, and training simulators.

Style: Clean, professional look that fits into any modern interior.

results.name: Etruscan jug or oinochoe
results.description:
Culture: [Etruscan](http://vocab.getty.edu/page/aat/300020471) Material: Bronze Dims: H 24.5 x D (of base) 8.25 Accession No: HCA 679 Current Location: [The Hunt Museum](https://www.huntmuseum.com/), [Limerick](https://www.geonames.org/7778675/limerick-city.html). 

A bronze Etruscan [oinochoe](http://vocab.getty.edu/page/aat/300198866) or jug with an upward flanged spout, slightly tapered body and flattened foot. The rim has snake-headed terminals and the handle has foliate decoration at the base. [More](https://www.huntmuseum.com/explore/item/700e47e2-a414-39c0-b722-f4028c5931ed/?s%3Detruscan&pos=1).

results.name: Penannular Ring-Brooch Mould
results.description:
Culture: [Early Christian](http://n2t.net/ark:/99152/p0ff3dt3t2p) Material: Soapstone Dims: H 6.1cm W 5.9cm Accession No: HCA 686 Current Location: [The Hunt Museum](https://www.huntmuseum.com/) [Limerick](https://www.geonames.org/7778675/limerick-city.html) A valve with moulds for penannular [ring-brooches](http://vocab.getty.edu/page/aat/300263352) on both sides. One negative is for a ribbed ring with slightly expanded, triangular terminals. Pouring channels are located at the terminal ends. Depressions in two corners indicate where other valve was secured. The reverse has a negative for a plain ring with spheroid terminals and a smaller ring with small spheroid terminals. Pouring channels are visible for both. There is an [ogham](http://vocab.getty.edu/page/aat/300263074) inscription on one edge.
[More](https://www.huntmuseum.com/explore/item/7d99dca4-fd93-39f1-b7de-aa0c18a1778d/?s%3Dmould&pos=9)

results.name: Crucifix
results.description:
Culture: Italian. | Material: [Wood; Rosewood](https://www.getty.edu/vow/AATFullDisplay?find=rosewood&logic=AND&note=&english=N&prev_page=1&subjectid=300012424); [Wood; Boxwood (gilded).](https://www.getty.edu/vow/AATFullDisplay?find=Boxwood&logic=AND&note=&english=N&prev_page=1&subjectid=300012002) | Accession No: [HCM 066](https://www.huntmuseum.com/explore/item/47ed96c4-2a96-36e8-8182-955273aa0850/?s%3DHCM+066&pos=1). | Current Location: [The Hunt Museum Limerick](https://www.huntmuseum.com). | Dimensions (cm): H 114 x W 53.

Description:
A Crucifix in rosewood with boxwood corpus. There are ornate gilt metal terminals on the cross arms and upper shaft. The base is hexagonal. The crucifix figure has a short flowing loin-cloth, a crown of thorns and the feet nailed together. There is a INRI plaque over the head and there was an ivory skull attached below the feet, this is now missing. This piece was probably made by Andrea Fantoini of Bergamo, Italy.

Date Made: H 114 x W 53

results.name: Tomb of Elizabeth Norris
results.description: Chest tomb to Elizabeth Norris, with effigy c.1779. Portland stone. Semi-reclining effigy of a veiled woman contemplating an urn, placed upon a chest with fielded inscription panels, and set within original cast-iron railings with obelisk finials to the rails and flaming urn terminals to the principal posts. Also to her husband Richard Norris of Hampstead (d.1779). A rare example of an external churchyard monument with an effigy.

results.name: WAW-49C525 - Purse bar
results.description:
An incomplete, copper alloy Medieval to Post Medieval purse bar dating c. AD 1450-1550.

The object consists of the remnants of a purse bar with a globular terminal. The purse bar has a rectangular cross section (4.29mm wide, 3.38mm thick), and curves slightly upwards and leftwards around halfway along the length of the remaining section of the bar, before it starts to arc towards the right. The terminal is globular in shape with a length of 8.09mm, width of 10.56mm, and thickness of 9.83mm. The terminal is decorated with six irregularly sized engraved twisting grooves.

To read more about this object, head to the Portable Antiquities Scheme page here: https://finds.org.uk/database/artefacts/record/id/1089004

results.name: Wmid-bd7bb4 Post Medieval end cap or pommel
results.description:
A complete copper-alloy terminal, 'end-cap' or pommel from a knife of Post Medieval dating (AD 1500 to AD 1600).

This terminal is likely to have come from an iron scale tang knife. The terminal is in the form of a human head wearing a pointed hat or helmet with multiple vertically engraved lines perhaps suggesting hair with a double-banded ruff around the neck. The face comprises of two circular indents for eyes, a protruding, pointed nose, now partially worn, and a straight groove for the mouth. There is a slot for a tang at the base, extending up the length of the neck, which contains the remains of the iron tang.

To find out more, visit the Portable Antiquities Scheme database: https://finds.org.uk/database/artefacts/record/id/1119838
